newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat Podravka's 96 results delayed by reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Croat Podravka's 96 results delayed by reshuffle.

text.p: Croatia's largest food group Podravka may delay releasing its 1996 results because of plans to reshuffle top managers, a well-informed source close to the company said on Wednesday.
"There is much talk about who will replace the current chief executive, but no decision has been reached yet," said the source who spoke on condition of anonymity.
"Results will probably be published together with a new business plan, and everyone seems to think it should be announced by the person in charge of implementing it," he said.

A revamped business strategy, created in consultation with international advisers Arthur D. Little, is crucial to setting Podravka on the path to profitability after it sold some loss-making subsidiaries at the end of 1996.
The group posted a net loss of 135 million kuna in 1995 but said it would return to profit soon after the divestiture and restructuring of old debts.
Last year's results were due to come out in May but the date has now been postponed till June at the earliest, the source said.

Recent rumours that a substantial consolidated loss for 1996 would be disclosed have dragged down the price of Podravka's shares on the Zagreb bourse, where they trade in a segment for semi-regulated companies.
They bottomed out at 260 kuna on Tuesday after sliding continuously for several weeks. It reached a 1997 high of 400 kuna in January.

But the source said the parent company's performance had been positive and any losses were attributable to the non-core units sold in 1996. "If you take those off the accounts, the group loss is not so large." -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
